observations: Photo 0 shows an industrial sewing machine on a white table with a thread stand, multiple thread spools, a motor mounted underneath, and a foot pedal on the floor.
Photo 1 shows the same machine setup from a similar angle with a watermark across the image.
Photo 2 shows an angled view of the machine head, table surface with illegible red lettering, scissors, and small accessories on the table.
Photo 3 shows the full machine setup again with floor clutter and power cords visible.

claims.evidence: No readable brand or model plate is visible in photos 0-3; the red lettering on the table in photo 2 is not legible as EMel or EM 8500.

risks.risk: The machine may not run or stitch properly.
risks.proof: A video of the machine powered on and stitching a piece of fabric.

risks.risk: The brand or model may not be EMel EM 8500.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of any brand plate or label on the machine head or table.
risks.if_unproven: as a generic industrial sewing machine

risks.risk: Accessories such as bobbins, presser feet, pedal, or oil may be missing.
risks.proof: A photo showing all items included with the machine.

proof_requests: Close-up of any brand or model plate on the sewing machine head or table.
Video of the machine running and stitching a piece of fabric.
Photo showing all accessories included, such as bobbins, feet, pedal, oil, and manual.
response.reason: The photos show an industrial sewing machine on a stand with motor, but the seller's EMel EM 8500 claim cannot be read from any photo, so it is priced as an unverified industrial machine at worst case.
